previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a complex history including common variable immunodeficiency, prior primary colonic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, EBV-positive nodular sclerosis Hodgkin lymphoma status post allogeneic stem cell transplant, and graft-versus-host disease was readmitted for treatment of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus pneumonia identified on bronchoalveolar lavage. She was afebrile and breathing comfortably on room air during admission. Vancomycin was initiated and adjusted based on trough levels, with dose reduction due to nephrotoxicity concerns; IV fluids were given to support renal function. A cardiac MRI ruled out endocarditis. Her transplant-related medications were maintained with therapeutic monitoring. She remained in remission from lymphoma. Psychiatric symptoms related to duloxetine discontinuation were addressed with medication restart and outpatient follow-up planning. She improved clinically and was discharged home with a visiting nurse to complete intravenous vancomycin and supportive care.

Dear Ms. ___,
It was a pleasure participating in your healthcare at ___ 
___. You came to us with bleeding 
from your ostomy site and increased output from your stoma that 
was watery and malodorous. In the emergency room you were 
evaluated by the sugical team who found the site of bleeding at 
the 6 o'clock position at the base of your ostomy where it
